simple: A queue is a line of items where the first one in is the first one out, just like a line at a snack stand. Games use queues for things like players waiting for a match or tasks waiting their turn. There is also a priority queue, where more important items jump ahead. Luau does not have a queue type built in, but you can make one with a table.
analogy: A regular queue is the line for a ride: whoever got there first gets on first. A priority queue is like a line where VIP pass holders get to go ahead of everyone else.
keyPoints: A regular queue follows FIFO: first in, first out.
New items are added to the back, and items are read or removed from the front.
In a priority queue, each item has a priority number. Higher priority items come out first.
In a priority queue, a new item goes behind all items with the same or higher priority. To jump to the very front, give it a higher priority than the current highest.
Priority queues help with matchmaking, for example giving players who waited longest a higher priority.
`MemoryStoreService` has built-in queues for sharing data across servers. For anything else, build a queue with a table.
The page's queue module has `enqueue` (add to back), `dequeue` (take from front), and `isEmpty`.

terms.queue: A list where items join at the back and leave from the front.
terms.FIFO: First In, First Out. The item added first is the first one removed.
terms.enqueue: To add an item to the back of the queue.
terms.dequeue: To remove the item at the front of the queue.
terms.priority queue: A queue where items with bigger priority numbers come out first, no matter when they were added.
terms.priority: A number that says how important an item is. With priorities 0, 3, and 5, the 5 comes out first.
terms.linear data structure: Items arranged in a single line, one after another.
terms.MemoryStoreService: A Roblox service for short-term data shared between all your game's servers. It includes built-in queues.
terms.ModuleScript: A script that holds code other scripts can load with `require`.

example.title: A simple waiting line for a mini-game
example.code:
-- A simple queue using a table and two counters
local queue = {}
local first = 1 -- position of the front item
local last = 0  -- position of the back item

local function enqueue(value)
	last += 1
	queue[last] = value
end

local function isEmpty()
	return first > last
end

local function dequeue()
	if isEmpty() then
		return nil
	end
	local value = queue[first]
	queue[first] = nil -- clear the old spot
	first += 1
	return value
end

enqueue("Ava")
enqueue("Ben")
enqueue("Cho")

print(dequeue()) --> Ava (first in, first out)
print(dequeue()) --> Ben
enqueue("Dev")
print(dequeue()) --> Cho
print(dequeue()) --> Dev
print(dequeue()) --> nil (the line is empty)
explain: `first` and `last` remember where the front and back of the line are.
`enqueue` moves `last` up by 1 and puts the new name there.
`dequeue` takes the name at `first`, clears that spot, and moves `first` up by 1.
Names come out in the same order they went in: Ava, Ben, Cho, then Dev.
When the line is empty, `dequeue` returns `nil` instead of crashing.

watchOut: Removing from an empty queue. Check `isEmpty()` first, or the page's module will throw an error.
Using `table.remove(list, 1)` on very long lists. It shifts every item, which gets slow; the two-counter method avoids that.
Mixing up queues and stacks. A queue gives you the oldest item; a stack gives you the newest.
